overall_delta.quality_improvement: Skill: Structured deliberation, explicit persona positions, confidence gates, dissent tracking. Baseline: Traditional analysis approach. Both valid; skill better for org alignment and explicit tradeoff visibility.

analyst_observations: All assertions pass for both skill and baseline—both approaches are competent.
Skill's key differentiation: (1) Quantified consensus strength (enables min-confidence gates), (2) Explicit persona dissent, (3) Structured cross-examination insights
Baseline's key strength: Faster execution, practical recommendations with actionable conditions, similar depth of analysis for business decisions
Eval 2 telemetry: Skill rejected (23% vs 70% threshold); baseline approved (72%). Skill's lower confidence reflects genuine split—Devil's Advocate and Logician both flag unproven business value.
Eval 3 free-tier: Skill shows 4% consensus (highly split); baseline pragmatic ('proceed with caution'). Skill quantifies risk; baseline absorbs it.
Token cost: Skill averages +77% tokens vs baseline, primarily from detailed persona deliberation.
Duration note: Baseline runs <40s consistently; skill with-skill runs show high variance due to subagent timing in iterations 2-3 (likely measurement artifacts; actual deliberation is <2min).
Recommendation: Skill is ready for use. Both approaches coexist: skill for high-stakes decisions needing quorum visibility; baseline for fast iteration/low-stakes decisions.
